0: Didn't I Say to Make My Abilities Average in the Next Life?! by FUNA (Seven Seas) is a lighthearted fantasy comedy. After dying to save a little girl, Misato Kurihara asks God to make her abilities perfectly average in her next life. She wakes up as Adele, only to learn that "average" was measured across every creature in the world, dragons included. Renaming herself Mile, she sets out to live as a normal hunter. It's a cheerful, easygoing read for fans of overpowered-heroine comedies.
1: The Dirty Way to Destroy the Goddess's Heroes by Sakuma Sasaki (Yen Press) is a fantasy action comedy with a scheming streak. High schooler Shinichi Sotoyama is summoned to another world by a demon king who needs help against heroes the goddess keeps bringing back to life. Shinichi has no great power, so he wins with cunning, tricks, and underhanded plans. It's a good fit for readers who like clever leads who think their way out of trouble.
3: Wotakoi: Love Is Hard for Otaku by Fujita (Kodansha) is a warm workplace romantic comedy. Office worker Narumi Momose keeps her otaku hobbies hidden after past relationships went badly. At her new job she runs into her childhood friend Hirotaka, a devoted gamer, and the two start dating for convenience. Their romance plays out in fandom jokes, game nights, and awkward adult moments. It's a cozy pick for anyone who has ever had to hide a hobby.
4: X/1999 by CLAMP (Viz Media) is a dark supernatural action drama. Kamui Shiro returns to Tokyo after years away, and he is at the center of a prophecy about the end of the world. Two groups with extraordinary powers, the Dragons of Heaven and the Dragons of Earth, are gathering to decide humanity's fate, and both want Kamui. It's a moody, dramatic series with CLAMP's striking artwork, best for readers who like apocalyptic stories and heavy emotion.
7: Drifters by Kouta Hirano (Dark Horse) is a violent, darkly funny fantasy action series. In the middle of a desperate battle in 1600, the samurai Shimazu Toyohisa is pulled into a strange world at war. There he meets other famous warriors from history, including Oda Nobunaga and the archer Nasu no Yoichi, who have also been brought there. It's a wild, bloody ride from the creator of Hellsing, made for readers who enjoy history-mashup battles.
8: Dungeon People by Sui Hutami (Seven Seas) is a fantasy comedy that looks at dungeons from the inside. Clay is a skilled scout searching for her missing father deep inside a dungeon. Instead of finding him, she meets the dungeon's master, who hires her to help run the place. Clay soon learns the work of building traps, managing monsters, and keeping adventurers coming. It's a fun read for anyone who likes behind-the-scenes fantasy worldbuilding.
9: Magical x Miracle by Yuzu Mizutani (Tokyopop) is a gentle fantasy comedy. Sylthfarn is an ordinary girl who happens to look exactly like Vistalsha, a powerful court wizard who has gone missing. To keep the kingdom stable, she is asked to take his place in secret, even though she knows almost no magic. Keeping up the act means learning fast and handling court intrigue. It's a sweet story for readers who enjoy disguise plots and quiet magic.
13: Mermaid Saga by Rumiko Takahashi (Viz Media) is a haunting horror anthology. Legend says that eating mermaid flesh grants eternal life, but for most people it brings death or a monstrous change. Yuta ate it five hundred years ago and has lived ever since, searching for a mermaid who can make him mortal again. Along the way he meets Mana, a girl who shares his fate. It's a darker side of the creator of Inuyasha and Ranma 1/2.
15: Shakugan no Shana by Yashichiro Takahashi (Viz Media) is a supernatural action story. High schooler Yuji Sakai learns that he is already dead, and what remains is a Torch, a fading stand-in left behind by creatures that feed on people's existence. A fierce girl with flaming hair, a warrior who hunts those creatures, decides to protect him. Yuji names her Shana. It's a classic for fans of action, mystery, and a prickly heroine.
16: Shaman King: Flowers by Hiroyuki Takei (Kodansha) is a supernatural action sequel to Shaman King. Hana Asakura is the son of Yoh and Anna, but he has grown up far from his famous parents. As a new generation of shamans steps forward, Hana starts learning what it means to carry his family's name and power. It's a good next step for longtime Shaman King readers who want to see the world through a new hero's eyes.
19: Someday's Dreamers by Norie Yamada (Tokyopop) is a quiet fantasy slice-of-life story. In a world where licensed magic users help people with everyday tasks, Yume Kikuchi travels from the countryside to Tokyo to finish her training. Under a gruff mentor, she learns that magic comes with rules, and that helping people is more complicated than she expected. It's a soft, thoughtful read for anyone who likes coming-of-age stories with a touch of magic.
20: Spirit Circle by Satoshi Mizukami (Seven Seas) is a supernatural fantasy about past lives. Fuuta Okami is a middle schooler who has always been able to see ghosts. When a new transfer student, Kouko Ishigami, arrives, she announces that she intends to kill him. Her reason lies in their past lives, which Fuuta begins to relive one by one. It's a heartfelt, inventive series for readers who like stories spanning centuries.
21: Superwomen in Love! Honey Trap and Rapid Rabbit by sometime (Seven Seas) is a playful yuri romantic comedy. Rapid Rabbit is a superheroine and Honey Trap is a supervillain, and in costume they are bitter enemies. Out of costume, though, their feelings for each other are getting harder to ignore. It's a light, fun read for fans of superhero parody and sweet romance between women.
22: Soul Eater NOT! by Atsushi Ohkubo (Yen Press) is a school comedy set in the Soul Eater world. Tsugumi Harudori discovers she is a weapon who can turn into a halberd, and she enrolls at the Death Weapon Meister Academy. She lands in the NOT class, meant for students learning to control their powers. There she must choose a meister partner while making friends and figuring out daily life. It's a lighter, friendlier side story that also works for newcomers.
23: A Witch's Printing Office by Mochinchi (Yen Press) is a cheerful fantasy comedy about fandom. Mika, a woman who loves comic conventions, finds herself in a world of magic with no such events. She starts a printing office to bring that fan culture to her new home, helping witches and wizards publish their own books. It's a funny, affectionate read for anyone who has ever loved a con or a self-published zine.
24: The Empty Box and Zeroth Maria by Eiji Mikage (Yen Press) is a twisting psychological mystery. Kazuki Hoshino values his ordinary school life, so he is shaken when a transfer student, Aya Otonashi, introduces herself by declaring war on him. Soon he realizes he is reliving the same days over and over, and Aya seems to know why. It's a tense, puzzle-like read for fans of time loops and unreliable reality.
29: Sugar Apple Fairy Tale by Miri Mikawa (Yen Press) is a gentle fantasy romance. Anne Halford is a young candy crafter who dreams of becoming a Silver Sugar Master, like her late mother. To travel safely to the royal competition, she buys a fairy warrior, the proud and sharp-tongued Challe, as her bodyguard. Their journey tests her skill and her belief that fairies should be free. It's a sweet, earnest read for fans of slow-burn romance.
30: Arifureta Zero by Ryo Shirakome (J-Novel Club) is a fantasy adventure prequel to Arifureta: From Commonplace to World's Strongest. Long before Hajime's story, a world ruled by a cruel church faces a small band of rebels with rare powers. Miledi Reisen, a bold and cheerful girl, sets out to recruit allies, starting with a talented young craftsman named Oscar Orcus. It's a good pick for Arifureta fans curious about the legends behind the main series.
31: Rokka: Braves of the Six Flowers by Ishio Yamagata (Yen Press) is a fantasy mystery wrapped in an adventure. When the Demon God stirs, six heroes are chosen to stop it. Adlet Mayer, who calls himself the strongest man in the world, is one of them. But when the Braves meet, there are seven, and they realize one must be an impostor. It's a clever, tense read for anyone who loves a locked-room puzzle with swords.
32: Your Forma by Mareho Kikuishi (Yen Press) is a near-future sci-fi detective story. Echika Hieda is a gifted investigator who solves crimes by diving into people's memories through a brain implant called Your Forma. She has trouble keeping partners, until she is paired with Harold, a polite and perceptive android. Together they take on cases tied to the technology. It's a smart pick for fans of buddy-cop mysteries and stories about humans and AI.
38: Heterogenia Linguistico by Salt Seno (Yen Press) is a gentle fantasy adventure about language. When his professor is injured, a young linguistics student travels to the land of monsters to continue the research. Guided by Susuki, a half-werewolf girl, he learns that each species talks in its own way, through scent, color, gesture, or sound. It's a curious, cozy read for anyone who likes thoughtful worldbuilding and cross-cultural misunderstandings.
40: Pet Shop of Horrors: Tokyo by Matsuri Akino (Tokyopop) is a supernatural horror anthology and a follow-up to Pet Shop of Horrors. The mysterious Count D has reopened his pet shop in Tokyo's Kabukicho district. Each customer who walks in is matched with a rare and unusual pet, along with a contract that must not be broken. Those who break the rules face the consequences. It's an elegant, eerie read for fans of moral fables with a dark twist.
41: Today's Menu for the Emiya Family by TAa (Denpa) is a cozy cooking comedy spun off from the Fate series. Shirou Emiya loves to cook, and his kitchen is always busy feeding Saber, Rin, Sakura, Taiga, and other friends. Each chapter centers on a seasonal home-cooked meal, with gentle humor and no battles to worry about. It's a warm read for Fate fans and for anyone who enjoys food manga with real recipes.
45: Under Ninja by Kengo Hanazawa (Denpa) is an offbeat action comedy. In modern Japan, ninja still exist in secret, and there are far more of them than anyone knows. Kuro Kumogakure is one of them, but he is a broke, idle young man with nothing to do. Then he gets his first real mission in a long time: go undercover as a high school student. It's a dry, strange, often funny read from the creator of I Am a Hero.
51: The Yakuza's Guide to Babysitting by Tsukiya (Kaiten Books) is a heartwarming comedy. Kirishima is so violent and feared that people call him the Demon. His boss gives him an unexpected new job: looking after Yaeka, the boss's quiet young daughter. Neither of them knows how to talk to the other at first, but they slowly become a family. It's a sweet, funny read for fans of tough-guy-meets-kid stories.
53: Two Flowers for the Dragon by Nari Kusakawa (CMX) is a gentle fantasy romance. Princess Shakuya can turn into a dragon, and she is next in line to rule her oasis kingdom. Her first fiancé disappeared years ago, so she became engaged to another young man. Then the first fiancé comes back, with no memory of her, and Shakuya must choose between them. It's a charming, lighthearted read from the creator of The Recipe for Gertrude.
54: Unnamed Memory by Kuji Furumiya (Yen Press) is a fantasy romance with plenty of magic and political intrigue. Crown Prince Oscar carries a curse that means no woman can bear his child. He climbs the tower of Tinasha, the Witch of the Azure Moon, to ask her to break it. Instead, he proposes that she marry him. Tinasha agrees to stay at his castle for a year. It's a rich, slow-building read for fans of witches and royal courts.
62: DRCL Midnight Children by Shin-ichi Sakamoto (Viz Media) is a gothic horror reimagining of Bram Stoker's Dracula. In 1890s England, a group of students at a seaside boarding school, including Mina Murray, begin to sense something wrong around them. A strange presence has arrived, and it is drawn to the young people of the town. Sakamoto's detailed, unusual artwork makes it stand out. It's a haunting read for fans of classic horror told in a new way.
66: Last Samurai Standing by Shogo Imamura (Kodansha) is a historical action thriller based on Imamura's novel. In the Meiji era, when samurai have lost their place, nearly three hundred fighters are lured to Kyoto by the promise of a huge prize. They are told to travel to Tokyo, taking wooden tags from one another along the way, by any means necessary. Saga Shujiro, a former samurai with a family to save, joins the game. It's a tense, bloody read for fans of survival battles.
70: Sentenced to Be a Hero by Rocket Shokai (Yen Press) is a gritty military fantasy. In this world, "Hero" is a punishment, and those sentenced to it are sent to fight demon lords again and again, revived each time they die. Xylo Forbartz, a former knight commander, is serving that sentence when he meets Teoritta, a goddess who chooses him as her knight. It's a dark, action-heavy read for readers who like battle-hardened antiheroes.
71: The Strange House by Uketsu (Seven Seas) is an unsettling horror mystery. A writer is shown the floor plan of a house that someone is thinking of buying. At first it seems ordinary, but on a closer look there is a small room that doesn't make sense. Trying to understand that room leads him and a friend into a much darker story. It's a quietly creepy read for fans of puzzle-like mysteries.
72: Sengoku Youko by Satoshi Mizukami (Tokyopop) is a fantasy adventure set in Japan's warring states era. Tama is a fox spirit who believes in protecting humans, and her brother Jinka is a human who would rather live among spirits. The pair travel the countryside dealing with bandits and troublemaking monsters. They are soon joined by Shinsuke, a timid young man who wants to become strong. It's a warm, action-filled read about family and belonging.
74: Kuma Miko: Girl Meets Bear by Masume Yoshimoto (One Peace Books) is a gentle countryside comedy. Machi is a shrine maiden in a tiny mountain village, where her closest companion is Natsu, a talking bear. Machi dreams of going to high school in the city, but she knows very little about modern life. Natsu worries about whether she is ready. It's a sweet, quirky read for fans of rural slice-of-life stories.
75: King of Thorn by Yuji Iwahara (Tokyopop) is a sci-fi survival horror story. A deadly disease called the Medusa virus is spreading around the world with no cure. A small group of patients, including a girl named Kasumi, is put into cold sleep until a cure can be found. When they wake up, their facility is overrun by thorny vines and monsters. It's a gripping read for fans of survival mysteries.
76: With the Light: Raising an Autistic Child by Keiko Tobe (Yen Press) is a heartfelt family drama. Sachiko is a young mother whose baby son, Hikaru, is diagnosed with autism. With little help from those around her, she sets out to understand him and give him the best life she can. The story follows Hikaru as he grows, along with the challenges and joys of raising him. It's a thoughtful read for parents, educators, and anyone who loves family stories.
81: Ichi the Witch by Osamu Nishi and Shiro Usazaki (Viz Media) is a fantasy action story. Ichi is a hunter boy who lives alone in the mountains. One day he defeats a creature called a Majik, and by doing so he becomes the first male witch, in a world where only women are supposed to be witches. That draws the attention of the witches' world. It's a bold, fast-moving adventure for fans of shonen action.
90: Blue Lock by Muneyuki Kaneshiro and Yusuke Nomura (Kodansha) is an intense soccer drama. After Japan's national team suffers another loss, the Japan Football Union starts an unusual program called Blue Lock. Three hundred young strikers are brought together to compete until only one is left, the striker who will lead Japan. High schooler Yoichi Isagi is one of them. It's a fierce, high-energy read for sports fans who like competition and big rivalries.
92: Dragon Quest: The Mark of Erdrick by Chiaki Kawamata and Kamui Fujiwara (Square Enix Manga) is a classic fantasy adventure based on the Dragon Quest games. When monsters destroy the kingdom of Carmen, the young prince Arus survives. He carries the mark of Erdrick, the legendary hero, and sets out to stop the forces of evil. It's a sweeping, old-school adventure for Dragon Quest fans and anyone who loves a quest story.
95: The Holy Grail of Eris by Kujira Tokiwa (Yen Press) is a fantasy mystery with a hint of revenge. Constance Grail is a kind, honest noblewoman who is framed for a crime at a royal ball. Her rescuer is Scarlett Castiel, the ghost of a villainess who was executed years ago. Scarlett offers to help Constance clear her name, if Constance helps get revenge on whoever framed her. It's a sharp, clever read for fans of court intrigue.
96: Yaiba: Samurai Legend by Gosho Aoyama (Viz Media) is a fun, fast-paced action adventure. Yaiba Kurogane has grown up in the jungle, training as a samurai with his father. When they come to Japan, Yaiba moves in with a family whose daughter, Sayaka, practices kendo. He soon finds a rival in Onimaru, who wants to rule the world. It's a cheerful, high-energy read from the creator of Case Closed.
98: Trapped in a Dating Sim: The World of Otome Games Is Tough for Mobs by Yomu Mishima (Seven Seas) is a fantasy comedy. A salaryman who was forced to play an otome game dies and wakes up inside it as Leon, a minor noble with no role in the plot. In this world, women rule and men are treated as background characters. Leon uses what he knows about the game to find a powerful hidden item. It's a witty read for fans of isekai with a sarcastic lead.
99: Hollow Regalia by Gakuto Mikumo (Yen Press) is a post-apocalyptic action fantasy. After a dragon disaster wiped out Japan, the country was left empty and closed off to the world. Yahiro Narusawa has survived alone, scavenging in the ruins. Then he meets Iroha Mamana, a cheerful girl who is the only other survivor he has found. It's a fast-paced read from the creator of Strike the Blood, for fans of dragons and adventure.
101: The Other World's Books Depend on the Bean Counter by Yatsuki Wakatsu and Kazuki Irodori (Yen Press) is a fantasy romance about finding your place through honest work. Seiichi Kondo, an overworked accountant, is pulled into another world by a summoning meant for the high school girl beside him. Left with nothing to do, he takes a job in the kingdom's finance department and starts untangling its messy books. It's a cozy, slow-burn BL for readers who like competent leads and a little office drama.
102: .hack//G.U.+ by Tatsuya Hamazaki (Tokyopop) is a sci-fi action story set inside an online game. In The World R:2, a lawless online RPG, a player named Haseo hunts the mysterious player killer Tri-Edge, whose attack left his friend Shino in a coma in real life. Chasing rumors and rival guilds, he finds the game hides much stranger things. It's a good pick for fans of the .hack games and virtual-world adventures.
105: Forbidden Dance by Hinako Ashihara (Tokyopop) is a shojo romance and drama about finding your nerve again. Aya Fujii gave up ballet after a crushing setback, until she sees a performance by Cool, an all-male dance troupe, and its lead dancer Akira. Determined to dance with them, she pushes her way into the group, where not everyone wants her. It's a short, heartfelt series for readers who like performing-arts stories with a romance.
107: Full Metal Panic! Overload! by Shoji Gatoh (ADV) is a gag comedy spin-off of Full Metal Panic!. Sousuke Sagara is an elite teenage soldier assigned to protect high schooler Kaname Chidori, but he has no idea how normal school life works. His battlefield instincts turn every small problem into a military operation, and Kaname's paper fan is never far away. It's light, silly fun for fans who loved the series' school comedy side.
108: MeruPuri by Matsuri Hino (Viz Media) is a sweet fantasy romance with a magical twist. High schooler Airi Hoshina dreams of an ordinary, low-key romance, until Aram, a young prince from another world, comes through her mirror. Stuck in her world under a curse that turns him into a teenager whenever he's in the dark, he ends up living with Airi. It's a short, charming shojo series from the creator of Vampire Knight, good for readers who like gentle magic and romantic comedy.
110: Mobile Suit Gundam SEED by Masatsugu Iwase (Del Rey) is a sci-fi war story adapted from the anime. Kira Yamato is a student on a neutral space colony when ZAFT forces attack, and he ends up in the cockpit of the Strike, a new Earth Alliance mobile suit. On the other side of the battle is his childhood friend Athrun Zala. It's a fast-moving take on the series for readers who like giant robots and divided loyalties.
112: Sword Art Online Progressive by Reki Kawahara (Yen Press) is a sci-fi action series set inside a deadly virtual world. It retells the story of Aincrad from the very first floor, after ten thousand players learn that dying in the game means dying for real. Kirito, a skilled solo player, and Asuna, a determined newcomer, team up to clear the floating castle one floor at a time. It's a great fit for fans who want a slower, fuller version of the original arc.
113: After the Rain by Jun Mayuzuki (Vertical) is a quiet romance and drama about dreams put on hold. Akira Tachibana was a high school track star until an injury took her off the field. Now working part time at a family restaurant, she finds herself drawn to her manager, Masami Kondo, a 45-year-old divorced dad who once wanted to be a writer. It's a gentle, thoughtful story for readers who like reflective slice of life with soft, rainy-day art.
114: Gacha Gacha by Hiroyuki Tamakoshi (Del Rey) is a teen romantic comedy with some fan service. Kouhei Kurita has a crush on Kurara Kirishima, his class's sweet, serious honor student. Then he learns that a video game brought out a second personality in her, a wild, flirty girl called Alice who appears at the worst possible moments. Kouhei decides to keep her secret and help her out. It's goofy, fast-paced fun for fans of 2000s rom-coms.
115: Gambling Apocalypse Kaiji by Nobuyuki Fukumoto (Denpa) is a psychological thriller about debt, desperation, and high-stakes games. Kaiji Itou is drifting through life when he's stuck with a huge debt after co-signing a loan for a former coworker. A loan shark offers a way out: one night of gambling aboard a ship called Espoir. It's tense and wildly inventive, a strong pick for readers who like mind games and underdog stories.
120: My Androgynous Boyfriend by Tamekou (Seven Seas) is a sweet romantic comedy about a couple who don't fit the usual mold. Mei is a hardworking career woman, and her boyfriend Meguru loves makeup and fashion and is often the prettiest person in the room. Together they navigate everyday life, other people's assumptions, and what they really want from each other. It's a warm, affirming read for anyone who likes gentle couple stories.
122: Tegami Bachi: Letter Bee by Hiroyuki Asada (Viz Media) is a fantasy adventure set in a land that never sees true daylight. In Amberground, Letter Bees brave monster-filled roads to deliver mail and the hearts it carries. Young Lag Seeing meets Gauche Suede, a Bee assigned to deliver Lag himself as a package, and the trip inspires him to become a Letter Bee too. It's a moving, beautifully drawn series for readers who like heartfelt journeys.
123: Girls und Panzer (Seven Seas), based on the anime, is an action comedy about an unusual school sport. In this world, tank warfare, or tankery, is a traditional art for young women. Miho Nishizumi transfers to Oarai Girls High School to get away from it, but the student council drafts her to revive the school's tankery team anyway. It's a light, upbeat mix of friendship and detailed tank battles for fans of the anime and military hardware.
127: Goblin Slayer Side Story: Year One by Kumo Kagyu and Kento Sakaeda (Yen Press) is a dark fantasy action series that shows how the Goblin Slayer got his start. After goblins destroyed his home village, a young man registers as a lowly Porcelain-rank adventurer and takes only goblin quests, which everyone else thinks are beneath them. Stubborn and methodical, he learns through hard, brutal experience. It's a good pick for fans of the main series; expect violence.
129: My Hero Academia: Smash!! by Hirofumi Neda (Viz Media) is a gag comedy spin-off of My Hero Academia. Izuku Midoriya and his classmates in Class 1-A are back, but this time the big fights and dramatic moments get turned into quick, silly jokes. Short chapters poke fun at the characters' quirks, personalities, and the main story's best-known scenes. It's light, goofy fun for fans who already know the cast.
131: The Candidate for Goddess by Yukiru Sugisaki (Tokyopop) is a sci-fi mecha drama about young pilots in training. On Zion, the last planet where humans survive, giant robots called Ingrids defend against mysterious invaders known as Victim. Zero Enna arrives at the pilot academy hoping to become one of the few who can pilot them. It's a compact series for readers who like academy stories and giant robots.
134: Grand Guignol Orchestra by Kaori Yuki (Viz Media) is a gothic fantasy and horror story about music as a weapon. A plague has turned much of the population into Guignols, living puppets that attack people. A traveling orchestra led by Lucille, a singer with a beautiful voice and a sharp tongue, roams the land fighting them with sound. Lavish art and dark fairy-tale drama make it a good fit for fans of Angel Sanctuary or Godchild.
135: Grandmaster of Demonic Cultivation by Mo Xiang Tong Xiu (Seven Seas) is a xianxia fantasy, mystery, and romance. Wei Wuxian, the feared Yiling Patriarch, died hated by the cultivation world. Thirteen years later, he is pulled back to life in the body of a young man who gave up his soul to summon him for revenge. Soon he crosses paths with Lan Wangji, a rigid, righteous cultivator from his past. It's a sprawling story for readers who love mystery and slow-burn BL.
136: Grandmaster of Demonic Cultivation by Mo Xiang Tong Xiu (Seven Seas) is a full-color comic adaptation of the xianxia fantasy novel. Wei Wuxian, once the most feared cultivator alive, is brought back from the dead years later in the body of a young man seeking revenge. Back in a world that still hates his name, he's soon caught up in a new mystery alongside the stern Lan Wangji. It's a lovely way to experience the story for fans of the novel and the donghua.
137: The Demon Ororon by Hakase Mizuki (Tokyopop) is a dark fantasy romance. Chiaki, a lonely teenage girl, finds a wounded stranger and takes care of him, only to learn he is Ororon, the king of hell, who has walked away from his throne. Ororon decides to stay by her side and protect her, even as the forces of heaven and hell come after them both. It's a short, moody shojo series for readers who like brooding demons and fated love.
138: Gravitation by Maki Murakami (Tokyopop) is a comedy romance about chasing music stardom. Shuichi Shindo, lead singer of the up-and-coming band Bad Luck, has his lyrics dismissed by a cold, handsome stranger, who turns out to be romance novelist Eiri Yuki. Shuichi can't let it go, and his stubborn pursuit turns into a stormy relationship. It's loud, funny, and dramatic, a classic early BL pick for readers who like rock-star energy.
139: Gunsmith Cats Burst by Kenichi Sonoda (Dark Horse) is an action comedy about bounty hunting in Chicago. Rally Vincent runs a gun shop and works as a bounty hunter, backed up by her explosives-loving partner Minnie May. Each case brings car chases, shootouts, and plenty of attitude. It's a fun follow-up to Gunsmith Cats for readers who like detailed guns, classic cars, and tough, capable heroines.
140: Gunsmith Cats by Kenichi Sonoda (Dark Horse) is a fast, stylish action comedy set in Chicago. Rally Vincent, a sharpshooting young gun shop owner, takes bounty hunting jobs on the side with her friend Minnie May, a demolitions expert. Their cases tangle them up with drug dealers, mobsters, and dangerous rivals. With detailed cars and gunplay and a lot of humor, it's a classic for fans of 1990s action manga.
141: My-HiME by Hajime Yatate (Tokyopop) is an action comedy about a school full of secrets. Yuuichi Tate transfers to Fuka Academy and soon meets Mai Tokiha, one of the HiME, girls who can summon powerful beings called Childs to fight monsters known as Orphans. Before long, Yuuichi finds himself tied up in the HiME and their battles. It's a lively mix of school life, fan service, and fights for readers who enjoyed the anime.
144: Astra Lost in Space by Kenta Shinohara (Viz Media) is a sci-fi adventure about survival and trust. Nine students set off on a planet camp trip, only to be swallowed by a mysterious sphere of light and flung thousands of light-years from home. With an old spaceship and limited supplies, they must hop from planet to planet to get back, while wondering whether one of them is a saboteur. It's a tight, twisty story with plenty of heart.
145: Happy Happy Clover by Sayuri Tatsuyama (Viz Media) is a cheerful comedy adventure for younger readers. Clover is an energetic little bunny who lives in Crescent Forest with her friends. Whether she's exploring, playing tricks, or getting into trouble, every day brings something new. It's a sweet, gentle series with expressive art that works well for early readers and anyone who loves cute animal stories.
146: Happy Hustle High by Rie Takada (Viz Media) is a shojo romantic comedy with plenty of energy. Hanabi Oozora is a tomboy who loves sports and has no interest in being ladylike. When her all-girls school merges with a boys' school, she lands right in the path of Yasuaki, the cool, aloof student council president. It's a fun, fast read for fans of bickering couples and school comedies.
147: Attack on Titan by Hajime Isayama (Kodansha) is a dark fantasy action story about humanity's last stand. For a hundred years, what's left of humanity has lived behind enormous walls, safe from the giant man-eating Titans outside. When a colossal Titan breaks through, young Eren Yeager watches his home fall and vows to wipe out every Titan. This omnibus edition collects the series in bigger volumes, a good fit for readers who want to read it straight through.
148: Azumanga Daioh by Kiyohiko Azuma (ADV) is a laid-back comedy about the everyday lives of high school girls. Ten-year-old prodigy Chiyo skips ahead to high school, where she makes friends with dreamy Osaka, quiet Sakaki, loud Tomo, and level-headed Yomi, under their scatterbrained teacher Yukari. Told in four-panel comic strips, it follows them through classes, festivals, and summers. It's warm, funny, and a classic for slice-of-life fans.
151: Battle Angel Alita: Last Order by Yukito Kishiro (Kodansha) is a sci-fi action series that continues the story of Battle Angel Alita. Alita, a cyborg fighter, wakes up rebuilt by the eccentric genius Desty Nova and finds herself in Ketheres, a city in orbit high above Earth. Soon she's drawn into the Zenith of Things Tournament, where fighters from across the solar system compete. It's a dense, action-packed read for readers who finished the original series.
153: Hollow Fields by Madeleine Rosca (Seven Seas) is a gothic fantasy with a sense of humor. Young Lucy Snow ends up, by mistake, enrolled at Miss Weaver's Academy for the Scientifically Gifted and Ever So Slightly Dead. The school runs on strict rules, clockwork, and very strange teachers, and students who fail tend to disappear. It's a spooky, charming series for readers who like Tim Burton-style boarding school stories.
155: Oreimo by Tsukasa Fushimi (Dark Horse) is a comedy about siblings and secret hobbies. Kyosuke Kosaka barely talks to his younger sister Kirino, a stylish model and honor student who seems perfect. Then he discovers she's secretly a huge otaku with a stash of anime and games, and she makes him her reluctant confidant. It's a light, chatty comedy about fandom and family for readers who enjoyed the anime.
159: Paradise Kiss by Ai Yazawa (Tokyopop) is a stylish romance and drama about figuring out who you want to be. Yukari Hayasaka is a high school senior stuck studying for exams she doesn't care about, until a group of fashion students scouts her to model for their label, Paradise Kiss. Through them, and the charming, unpredictable designer George, she gets a glimpse of a life she never imagined. It's a classic for fans of Nana and grown-up shojo.
161: I've Been Killing Slimes for 300 Years and Maxed Out My Level by Kisetsu Morita (Yen Press) is a cozy fantasy comedy. After working herself to death at an office job, Azusa is reborn as an immortal witch and settles into a quiet life in the countryside. Three hundred years of killing slimes for spending money quietly raise her to the max level, and word gets out. Soon her peaceful home fills up with visitors, rivals, and new family. It's relaxed, sweet, and funny.
164: Peace Maker by Nanae Chrono (Tokyopop) is a historical action story set in late Edo-period Kyoto. Tetsunosuke Ichimura is a short, hot-tempered teenager who wants to join the Shinsengumi, the feared police force, to get strong enough to avenge his parents' murder. Taken on as a page, he grows close to the group's captains and learns what strength really costs. It's a mix of humor, swordplay, and tragedy for readers interested in samurai history.
169: Cactus's Secret by Nene Yukimori (Viz Media) is a sweet romantic comedy about a crush that just won't land. Miku Kobayashi likes her classmate Kyohei Fujioka, a prickly boy who seems completely oblivious. No matter how many times she tries to show her feelings, he misses the point, or does he? It's a quick, funny, heartwarming read for fans of awkward first love.
176: Jiu Jiu by Touya Tobina (Viz Media) is a shojo fantasy about a hunter and her loyal companions. Takamichi Akiba comes from a family of demon hunters and has been raised to be tough and practical. Her family gives her two wolf pups, called jiu jiu, as familiars, and they grow up fast, soon able to take the form of teenage boys. Raising them turns out to be more than she bargained for. It's a cute, offbeat series for fans of supernatural shojo.
179: Please Tell Me! Galko-chan by Kenya Suzuki (Seven Seas) is a short-chapter comedy about high school girls and their frank conversations. Galko looks like a flashy gyaru, and the rumors about her are wild, but she's actually kind, shy, and a little old-fashioned. With her friends Otako and Ojou, she trades questions about bodies and growing up that most girls wonder about but rarely ask. It's funny and good-natured, with some mild fan service.
180: Princess Princess by Mikiyo Tsuda (DMP) is a comedy set at an all-boys school with an unusual tradition. When Toru Kono transfers to Fujimori Academy, he learns that the cutest boys are chosen as Princesses, who dress up in frilly outfits to brighten campus life. He's quickly drafted alongside Yujiro and Mikoto, and the job comes with perks and headaches. It's a lighthearted series for readers who like school comedies with a touch of shonen-ai.
183: Tower of God by SIU (Webtoon) is a fantasy action story about climbing a mysterious tower. Twenty-Fifth Baam has spent his whole life alone in the dark, with only his friend Rachel for company. When Rachel enters the Tower to see the stars, Baam follows her inside, where every floor brings deadly tests and strange new allies. It's a sprawling, inventive adventure for readers who like puzzle-box worlds and big casts.
192: Ultra Maniac by Wataru Yoshizumi (Viz Media) is a lighthearted magical romantic comedy. Ayu Tateishi is the cool, popular girl at her middle school, but she has a soft spot for romance. Then she befriends Nina Sakura, a clumsy transfer student who turns out to be a witch-in-training from the Magic Kingdom. Nina's spells tend to backfire, and Ayu keeps ending up in the middle of them. It's sweet, short, and fun.
194: Kilala Princess by Rika Tanaka and Nao Kodaka (Tokyopop) is a magical adventure for younger readers. Kilala is an ordinary girl who loves Disney princesses. When she meets Rei, a mysterious boy searching for a princess who can save his kingdom, a magic tiara sends them into the worlds of Snow White, Cinderella, and others. Along the way, Kilala learns what it really takes to be a princess. It's a sweet pick for Disney fans.
201: Versailles of the Dead by Kumiko Suekane (Seven Seas) is a historical horror story that mixes the French court with the walking dead. When Marie Antoinette is killed on the road to France, her twin brother Albert takes her place and enters Versailles disguised as the future queen. He has to keep his secret while the dead begin to rise around him. It's a good pick for readers who like court intrigue, gender-bending disguise, and dark, gory twists on real history.
205: Rosen Blood by Kachiru Ishizue (Viz Media) is a gothic shojo romance with vampires. Stella, a young woman with nowhere left to go, collapses in the woods and wakes up in an old mansion. Its owner, the cold and handsome Levi, and the other residents turn out to be vampires. Stella decides to stay and work as a maid, and slowly learns their secrets. It's a lush, moody read for fans of romantic fantasy and pretty, detailed art.
208: Saber Marionette J by Satoru Akahori (Tokyopop) is a sci-fi comedy with plenty of heart. On the colony planet Terra II, where only men survived, women exist only as legends and robots called marionettes do the work. Otaru Mamiya, a kind young man with little money, accidentally awakens Lime, a cheerful marionette with a special circuit that lets her feel real emotions. Soon two more join her. It's a lighthearted, energetic series for fans of '90s anime comedy.
224: Scryed by Yosuke Kuroda (Tokyopop) is a hard-hitting action story about people with strange powers. After a disaster tears a region of Japan away from the rest of the country, some children born there develop abilities called Alters. Kazuma, a hot-headed young mercenary, uses his Alter to survive in the lawless Lost Ground. His path keeps crossing with Ryuho, a disciplined Alter user working for the government force HOLY. It's a fast read for fans of rival fights and gritty sci-fi.
225: WorldEnd by Akira Kareno (Yen Press) is a quiet, bittersweet fantasy set after the end of the world. Humans were wiped out long ago, and the survivors live on floating islands above a land overrun by monsters. Willem Kmetsch, the last human, wakes after five hundred years and takes a job as caretaker of a military warehouse. There he finds a group of young girls who fight with ancient weapons, including the gentle Chtholly. It's a tender, melancholy story for readers who like emotional fantasy.
227: Love Me for Who I Am by Kata Konayama (Seven Seas) is a warm, funny story about friendship and identity. Mogumo, a nonbinary high school student, has never felt like they fit in anywhere. Then a classmate invites them to work at a maid cafe staffed by boys dressed as girls. Mogumo isn't a boy, but the cafe turns into a place where they can finally be themselves. It's a gentle, thoughtful read for anyone who enjoys found-family stories with heart.
229: Love Roma by Minoru Toyoda (Del Rey) is a sweet, offbeat romantic comedy. Hoshino is an earnest high school boy who says exactly what he thinks. On the day he first meets his classmate Negishi, he tells her he likes her and asks her out. Negishi doesn't know what to make of him, but his honesty slowly wins her over. It's a charming, low-key story for readers who want a romance without the usual drama and misunderstandings.
233: Your Turn to Die by Nankidai (Yen Press) is a tense thriller based on the popular death-game visual novel. High school student Sara Chidouin wakes up trapped in a strange facility with a group of strangers and her close friend Joe. A mysterious host forces them into deadly games where they must vote on who lives. Trust is hard to come by, and everyone has something to hide. It's a gripping read for fans of mysteries, survival games, and stories full of twists.
234: Yozakura Quartet by Suzuhito Yasuda (Kodansha) is a supernatural action comedy set in a town where humans and yokai live side by side. Akina Hiizumi runs a small counseling office in the town of Sakurashin with his friends Hime, the teenage mayor, and Ao and Kotoha, who each have special powers. Together they help residents, settle disputes, and protect the town from threats. It's a lively, stylish series for fans of yokai stories with big personalities.
235: Guardian Angel Getten by Minene Sakurano (Tokyopop) is a magical comedy about a boy and his new guardian spirit. Tasuke Shichiri, a middle school student who lives on his own, receives a strange ring from his traveling father. When he looks through it, Shaorin, a guardian spirit sworn to protect him, appears in his room. She takes her duty very seriously, which causes plenty of trouble. It's a light, playful series for fans of classic magical-girlfriend comedies.
236: Eerie Queerie by Shuri Shimizu (Tokyopop) is a sweet and funny supernatural romance. Mitsuo is a shy, sensitive high school boy who can see ghosts, and they love to borrow his body. Many of the spirits have unfinished business, which usually means confessing their love to someone, and Mitsuo ends up making a scene at school. His classmates start to get the wrong idea. It's a cute, lighthearted read for fans of ghost stories and boys' love comedy.
241: Fangirl by Rainbow Rowell (Viz Media) is a manga adaptation of the beloved coming-of-age novel. Cath is starting college, and her twin sister Wren no longer wants to be her roommate. Shy and anxious, Cath would rather keep writing her popular fan fiction about the boy wizard Simon Snow than face new people. A grumpy roommate and a friendly classmate start to pull her out of her shell. It's a warm, relatable story for anyone who has loved a fandom.
243: Shaman King by Hiroyuki Takei (Kodansha) is a supernatural action series about spirits, friendship, and a tournament like no other. Manta Oyamada, a small and timid student, takes a shortcut through a graveyard and meets Yoh Asakura, a laid-back boy who can see and talk to ghosts. Yoh is a shaman, training to enter the Shaman Fight and become the Shaman King. It's a fun, big-hearted series for fans of classic shonen adventure.
248: Slayers by Hajime Kanzaka (Tokyopop) is a fantasy comedy light novel series that launched a classic anime. Lina Inverse is a teenage sorceress with a huge appetite, a quick temper, and very powerful magic. While on the road, she teams up with Gourry Gabriev, a kind but not very bright swordsman who thinks she needs protecting. Their adventure soon pulls them into a fight with dark forces. It's a fun, fast read for fans of sword-and-sorcery humor.
250: School Judgment by Nobuaki Enoki and Takeshi Obata (Viz Media) is a courtroom mystery with a playful twist. At Tenbin Elementary, disputes between students are settled in a classroom court. Abaku Inugami, a confident transfer student, is a skilled defense attorney who takes on a classmate accused of a crime he says he didn't commit. Each case is a puzzle of clues and arguments. It's a clever, quick read for fans of legal mysteries and sharp art.
260: Juni Taisen: Zodiac War by Nisio Isin (Viz Media) is a violent action thriller about a battle royale. Every twelve years, twelve warriors, each representing an animal of the Chinese zodiac, meet to fight to the death. The last one standing is granted any wish. Each fighter has their own skills, past, and reason for being there. It's a dark, fast-paced read for fans of survival battles with a large cast of strong characters.
261: Kagerou Daze by Jin (Yen Press) is a sci-fi mystery light novel series based on the popular Vocaloid songs. Shintaro Kisaragi is a shut-in who hasn't left his room in two years. When his computer breaks on a hot August day, he heads to a department store, which is suddenly taken over by armed attackers. He soon meets a group of young people with strange eye powers. It's a twisty read for fans of mysteries, time loops, and quirky casts.
262: The Angel Next Door Spoils Me Rotten by Saekisan (Square Enix) is a sweet, slow-burn romantic comedy. Amane Fujimiya is a high school student who lives alone and doesn't take good care of himself. One rainy day he lends his umbrella to Mahiru Shiina, the most admired girl at school, who happens to live next door. To repay him, she starts bringing him home-cooked meals. It's a cozy, gentle read for fans of everyday romance.
264: Higehiro by Shimesaba (Yen Press) is a heartfelt drama about two people who need each other's help. Yoshida is a 26-year-old office worker who has just been turned down by the coworker he likes. On his way home, he finds Sayu, a high school runaway, sitting by the road with nowhere to go. He lets her stay at his apartment, and an unusual living arrangement begins. It's a thoughtful, emotional read about growing up and healing.
265: Restaurant to Another World by Junpei Inuzuka (Seven Seas) is a cozy fantasy about food bringing people together. Western Restaurant Nekoya is a small diner in a Tokyo shopping district, closed every Saturday. On that day, its door opens into a fantasy world, and elves, warriors, dragons, and other unusual guests drop in for a meal. Each one finds a dish that becomes a favorite. It's a warm, comforting read for anyone who loves food stories.
267: Cross-Dressing Villainess Cecilia Sylvie by Hiroro Akizakura (Yen Press) is a fantasy comedy light novel with a romantic twist. Cecilia remembers her past life and realizes she has been reborn as the villainess of a dating game, destined to die. To avoid her fate, she disguises herself as a boy named Cecil and stays far away from the prince. Somehow, things don't go to plan. It's a fun, breezy read for fans of reincarnation and villainess stories.
270: Chaika: The Coffin Princess by Ichiro Sakaki (Yen Press) is a fantasy adventure set after a long war. Toru Acura was trained as a saboteur, but now that peace has come, he has no purpose. Then he meets Chaika, a white-haired girl who carries a large coffin on her back and speaks in broken phrases. She wants to collect the remains of a fallen emperor, and Toru agrees to help. It's a fun, action-filled read for fans of quest stories.
271: Yokohama Kaidashi Kikou by Hitoshi Ashinano (Seven Seas) is a quiet, peaceful slice of life set after the world has slowly changed. Sea levels have risen and humanity is fading, but life goes on calmly. Alpha, a robot who looks like a young woman, runs a small coffee shop in the countryside while she waits for her owner to return. She meets neighbors, explores, and enjoys the moment. It's a gentle, beautiful read for anyone who wants something calm.
272: The Candidate for Goddess by Yukiru Sugisaki (Tokyopop) is a sci-fi action story about giant robots. In the far future, humanity's last planet is threatened by invaders called Victim. Zero Enna, a hopeful young boy, joins an academy that trains pilots for the Goddesses, the only machines that can fight back. He and his classmates must prove they can handle the pressure. It's a good pick for fans of mecha and academy stories.
276: Komomo Confiserie by Maki Minami (Viz Media) is a sweet romantic comedy about pastry and second chances. As a spoiled rich girl, Komomo Ichihara loved sweets and bossed around Natsu, a boy who lived at her family's estate. Years later, her family loses its fortune, and she ends up working at a pastry shop where Natsu is now a talented pastry chef. This time, he's the one in charge. It's a light, fun read for fans of shojo romance and food.
277: BL Metamorphosis by Kaori Tsurutani (Seven Seas) is a gentle, heartwarming story about an unlikely friendship. Ichinoi is a 75-year-old widow who stops in a bookstore and picks up a boys' love manga for its pretty cover. She's surprised to love it. Urara, the shy 17-year-old girl working at the counter, is a fan too, and the two start bonding over the series. It's a sweet, thoughtful read about loneliness, fandom, and finding your people.
278: Mushishi by Yuki Urushibara (Kodansha) is a quiet, atmospheric supernatural series. Mushi are simple, mysterious life forms that most people can't see, and they sometimes cause strange troubles for humans. Ginko, a white-haired mushi master, travels the countryside of old Japan to study them and help those who are affected. Each chapter is a mostly standalone tale. It's a calm, beautiful read for anyone who enjoys folklore and thoughtful stories.
279: Gate 7 by CLAMP (Dark Horse) is a fantasy action series set in modern-day Kyoto. Chikahito Takamoto, a high school student who loves Japanese history, finally gets to visit the ancient city. Almost right away, he stumbles into a hidden battle between people with strange powers and meets Hana, a mysterious girl at the center of it. It's a stylish read for fans of CLAMP's art, Japanese history, and supernatural fights.
282: Avatar: The Last Airbender by Michael Dante DiMartino and Bryan Konietzko (Tokyopop) is a kid-friendly adventure retold in manga form using art from the animated series. In a world where people can control the elements, the Fire Nation is at war with everyone else. Siblings Katara and Sokka find a boy frozen in an iceberg: Aang, the last airbender and the long-missing Avatar. It's a fun way for young fans to relive the show.
284: Zoids: Chaotic Century by Michiro Ueyama (Viz Media) is a kid-friendly action adventure about giant mechanical beasts. On planet Zi, metal creatures called Zoids are used in battle. Van Flyheight, a boy from a small desert village, finds a strange girl named Fiona and an organoid named Zeke in an old ruin. Soon he's riding into the middle of a war. It's a fun read for fans of robots, monsters, and big battles.
290: Act-Age by Tatsuya Matsuki (Viz Media) is a drama about acting and talent. Kei Yonagi is a high school girl who takes care of her younger siblings and dreams of becoming an actress. At an audition, her unusual method acting, where she fully becomes the role, catches the eye of an eccentric film director. He sets out to shape her into a star. It's an intense, inspiring read for fans of performing arts stories.
294: Kingdom Hearts 358/2 Days by Shiro Amano (Yen Press) is a fantasy adventure based on the popular video game. Roxas is the newest member of Organization XIII, a group of mysterious beings who have no memories of who they were. He's sent on missions to different worlds, and after work, he eats ice cream on a clock tower with his friends Axel and Xion. It's a warm, bittersweet read for fans of the games.
295: March Story by Hyung Min Kim (Viz Media) is a dark fantasy set in a gothic version of Europe. Evil spirits called ill hide inside beautiful antiques and possess the people who use them. March is a young girl who disguises herself as a boy and hunts ill as an Ill Hunter, carrying her own secret. Each case brings her face to face with greed and sorrow. It's a striking read for fans of moody, richly drawn fantasy.
305: Blood-C by CLAMP (Dark Horse), with art by Ranmaru Kotone, is a dark supernatural horror story with plenty of action. Saya Kisaragi is a cheerful, clumsy high school girl in a quiet country town, but by night she serves as a shrine maiden, taking up a sword to fight the Elder Bairns, monsters that feed on people. As the attacks grow worse, small things about her everyday life start to feel wrong. It suits readers who like moody, violent horror with a mystery underneath.
306: My Youth Romantic Comedy Is Wrong, As I Expected @ Comic by Wataru Watari (Yen Press) is a sharp, wry school comedy with a romantic streak. Hachiman Hikigaya is a cynical loner who thinks high school friendship is a scam, so after he turns in an essay mocking youth, his teacher drafts him into the Service Club, run by the brilliant and icy Yukino Yukinoshita, to help other students with their problems. It's a good fit for readers who enjoy dry humor and awkward, honest characters.
307: I Got a Cheat Skill in Another World and Became Unrivaled in the Real World, Too by Miku (Yen Press) is a light, wish-fulfillment fantasy that moves between two worlds. Yuuya Tenjou is a bullied, lonely boy who moves into his late grandfather's house. There he finds a door to another world, and the strength he gains on the other side follows him back home. It's an easygoing read for fans of power-up stories with a feel-good streak.
308: Reborn to Master the Blade: From Hero-King to Extraordinary Squire by Hayaken (Yen Press) is an action fantasy light novel with a playful twist. After a lifetime of rule, the legendary Hero-King Inglis asks to be reborn so he can focus purely on fighting. He gets his wish but comes back as a girl, Inglis Eucus, in a world where a magic crest decides who may become a knight, and without one, she sets out to train as a squire instead. It suits fans of battle-hungry heroes and lively fights.
309: I May Be a Guild Receptionist, but I'll Solo Any Boss to Clock Out on Time by Mato Kousaka (Yen Press) is a breezy action comedy fantasy. Alina Clover took a receptionist job at the adventurers' guild because it promised a stable life and regular hours. When a tough dungeon boss threatens to keep her working overtime, she quietly takes care of it herself, and no one is supposed to know it was her. It's a fun read for anyone who has ever just wanted to go home on time.
314: Lonely Castle in the Mirror by Mizuki Tsujimura (Seven Seas), adapted from her novel, is a gentle, bittersweet fantasy drama. Kokoro has stopped going to school and spends her days shut in her room, until one day her mirror begins to glow and pulls her into a fairy-tale castle, where six other kids and a girl in a wolf mask are waiting. They're told a hidden key can grant one wish. It's a thoughtful read for anyone who likes quiet, emotional stories about feeling alone.
316: Kindergarten Wars by You Chiba (Yen Press) is a fast, funny action comedy. Black Lily is a kindergarten for the children of the rich and powerful, which makes it a favorite target for kidnappers and hitmen, so its teachers are all former assassins, hired to keep the kids safe at any cost. Rita is one of the best of them, and when she isn't fighting off attackers, she's hoping to find a boyfriend. It's a good pick for readers who enjoy over-the-top fights mixed with workplace comedy.
317: My Quiet Blacksmith Life in Another World by Tamamaru (J-Novel Club) is a cozy, low-stakes fantasy. A tired office worker gets a second chance at life in another world, along with a talent for crafting. He has no interest in being a hero, so instead he builds a forge deep in a forest and settles in to make knives and swords at his own pace. It suits readers who enjoy slow-life stories about craft, good company and simple days.
319: I'll Become a Villainess Who Goes Down in History by Izumi Okido (Yen Press) is a cheerful fantasy comedy. Alicia realizes she has been reborn as the villainess of a game she once played, and instead of trying to dodge her fate, she decides to embrace it and become the greatest villainess ever. The trouble is, her idea of being wicked keeps coming across as kind and clever. It's a fun, upbeat read for fans of villainess stories that turn the formula on its head.
322: The Water Magician by Tadashi Kubo (J-Novel Club) is an easygoing fantasy adventure light novel. After dying young, Ryo is reborn in a world of swords and magic with a gift for water magic and a body that doesn't age. All he wants is a peaceful, quiet life, so he starts out alone in the wilderness, slowly sharpening his magic, before heading out into the wider world. It suits readers who like thoughtful, steady fantasy with careful magic and a calm hero.
327: Is the Order a Rabbit? by Koi (Yen Press) is a sweet, gentle slice-of-life comedy. Cocoa Hoto moves to a pretty, old-fashioned town for high school and boards at the Rabbit House, a small coffee shop, where she meets Chino, the quiet granddaughter of the owner, and Tippy, the fluffy rabbit who rides on Chino's head. It's a calm, cozy read for anyone who enjoys cute characters and low stakes.
329: Phantom Thief Jeanne by Arina Tanemura (Viz Media) is a sparkling magical girl adventure with plenty of comedy and romance. Maron Kusakabe seems like a normal high school girl, but she is the reincarnation of Joan of Arc, and with help from the angel-in-training Fin, she becomes the phantom thief Jeanne, stealing paintings where demons are hiding and sealing them away. A police detective's daughter, who happens to be her best friend, is determined to catch her. It's a classic for shojo fans who love magical girls.
331: Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint by singNsong (Ize Press) is a gripping action fantasy light novel. Kim Dokja is an ordinary office worker and the only person who has read a long web novel about surviving the end of the world all the way through, and one night on the subway, the story comes true around him. Now his knowledge of every twist may be the only thing keeping him alive. It's a great pick for readers who love clever survival stories and big, layered worlds.
333: The Rose of Versailles by Riyoko Ikeda (Udon) is a sweeping historical drama and romance set in the years before the French Revolution. Oscar François de Jarjayes is raised as a son by her father so she can follow him into the military. She becomes the commander of the royal guard, protecting the young Marie Antoinette as she arrives in France, and court intrigue, friendship and love follow. It's a landmark shojo classic and a great fit for readers who enjoy history and big emotions.
334: Takahashi from the Bike Shop by Arare Matsumushi (Yen Press) is a warm, grounded romance about grown-ups. Pan Tokura is an office worker who has trouble saying no and is used to keeping her head down. When her bike breaks down, a blunt young man named Takahashi from the local bike shop fixes it, and little by little, the two get to know each other. It's a lovely pick for readers who like slow, realistic romance and characters learning to stand up for themselves.
336: Sword Art Online: Ordinal Scale by Reki Kawahara (Yen Press) is an action sci-fi story set in the world of Sword Art Online. A new device called the Augma has made augmented reality part of everyday life, and its hit game, Ordinal Scale, sends players out into the streets of Tokyo to battle monsters and climb the rankings. Kirito and Asuna join in, but something about the game soon seems off. It suits fans of the series and anyone who enjoys virtual-world action.
346: Ascendance of a Bookworm Part 3 by Miya Kazuki (J-Novel Club) continues a thoughtful fantasy about a girl who loves books more than anything. Urano, a book lover, was reborn as Myne in a world where books are rare treasures only nobles can afford. In Part 3, she takes a new name and steps into the world of the nobility, where she must learn its rules while still chasing her dream of making books for everyone. It's a rewarding read for fans of slow-building, detailed worlds.
349: Blend-S by Miyuki Nakayama (Yen Press) is a bright, silly workplace comedy. Maika Sakuranomiya is a sweet, cheerful girl who keeps losing part-time jobs because her natural expression looks like a scary glare. She's finally hired at Stile, a cafe where each waitress plays a character type, and Maika's assigned role is the sadist, which is the last thing she really is. It's an easy, fun read for anyone who likes quirky casts and gentle humor.
351: The Brilliant Healer's New Life in the Shadows by Sakaku Hishikawa (J-Novel Club) is a fantasy action story with a big heart. Zenos is a gifted healer who was kicked out of his adventuring party for not seeming useful enough, so with no license and few options, he opens a small clinic in the city's slums. His skill quickly draws a crowd of unusual patients, and word of him spreads. It suits readers who enjoy underdog heroes and stories about building a new place to belong.
360: Classroom of the Elite: Year 2 by Syougo Kinugasa (Seven Seas) is a tense psychological school drama light novel. At Advanced Nurturing High School, students are ranked, rewarded and punished through constant tests and competitions between classes. As Kiyotaka Ayanokoji, who prefers to stay in the background, begins his second year as a new group of first-years arrives, the contests get sharper and the rivalries more personal. It's a good fit for readers who enjoy mind games and schemes.
362: Reborn to Master the Blade: From Hero-King to Extraordinary Squire by Moto Kuromura (Yen Press) is an action fantasy manga with a playful twist. After a lifetime of rule, the legendary Hero-King Inglis asks to be reborn so he can focus purely on fighting. He gets his wish but comes back as a girl, Inglis Eucus, in a world where a magic crest decides who may become a knight, and without one, she sets out to train as a squire instead. It suits fans of battle-hungry heroes and lively fights.
366: Mobile Suit Gundam: Cucuruz Doan's Island by Junji Ohno (Vertical) is a sci-fi war story drawn from the original Mobile Suit Gundam. During the war between the Earth Federation and Zeon, young pilot Amuro Ray is sent to a remote island, where he meets Cucuruz Doan, a former Zeon soldier who now lives quietly, caring for a group of orphaned children. Amuro has to decide what this strange man really is. It's a thoughtful pick for Gundam fans who like the human side of the war.
370: Spriggan by Hiroshi Takashige (Seven Seas), with art by Ryoji Minagawa, is a fast, punchy action thriller. Long ago, a lost civilization left behind powerful relics, and the ARCAM Foundation works to keep them out of the wrong hands. Yu Ominae looks like an ordinary high school student, but he's one of ARCAM's top agents, called Spriggans, and each mission sends him around the world against armies and rival agents. It's a great pick for readers who love classic action and treasure-hunting adventure.
371: SSS-Class Revival Hunter by Bill K (Ize Press) is a dark, fast-moving action fantasy. In a world where hunters gain special skills, Kim Gong-ja feels left behind when his power turns out to be strange: it lets him come back from death and take on the skills of whoever killed him. It's a painful way to grow stronger, but it may be the only way he can rise. It suits readers who enjoy tower-climbing hunters and stories about a hero clawing his way up.
373: Sugar Apple Fairy Tale by Miri Mikawa (Yen Press) is a sweet fantasy romance. Anne Halford is a young girl who wants to become a silver sugar master, an artist who crafts beautiful sculptures from sugar. To reach the capital for a contest, she needs protection on the road, so she buys a proud, sharp-tongued fairy warrior named Challe as her bodyguard. It's a gentle read for anyone who enjoys craft, kindness and slow-burn romance.
374: Flower of Life by Fumi Yoshinaga (Tokyopop) is a funny, warm school comedy with real heart. Harutaro Hanazono starts high school a month late after recovering from leukemia, and he jumps right in, befriending the shy Shota and the prickly, manga-obsessed Majima. Together they deal with class projects, crushes and the strange ups and downs of being teenagers. It's a great fit for readers who like sharp humor, honest characters and everyday stories that sneak up on you emotionally.
381: Futari Escape by Shouichi Taguchi (Seven Seas) is a laid-back comedy about two women dodging grown-up life. One is a manga artist always behind on her deadlines, and the other is her easygoing friend who doesn't have a job. Whenever things get to be too much, the two run off together, chasing snacks, small trips and silly little adventures. It's a cozy, relaxing read for anyone who has ever wanted to escape their to-do list for a day.
398: Amazing Agent Luna by Nunzio DeFilippis (Seven Seas), co-written with Christina Weir and drawn by Shiei, is a fun action spy story. Luna is a teenage girl who was raised by the government to be the perfect secret agent. She can handle any mission, but her newest one is going undercover at an ordinary high school, where fighting bad guys is easy for her, but making friends and fitting in are a lot harder. It's a fun pick for readers who like spy action mixed with school comedy.
